Add a 3D model layer to a Mapbox GL map

Source: R/model.R
add_model_layer.Rd

Draws one instance of a 3D model, registered with add_model(), at each point feature of a source. Mapbox GL JS only.

Usage

add_model_layer(
  map,
  id,
  source,
  model_id,
  source_layer = NULL,
  model_scale = NULL,
  model_rotation = NULL,
  model_translation = NULL,
  model_color = NULL,
  model_color_mix_intensity = NULL,
  model_opacity = NULL,
  model_emissive_strength = NULL,
  model_cast_shadows = NULL,
  model_receive_shadows = NULL,
  model_ambient_occlusion_intensity = NULL,
  model_type = NULL,
  model_elevation_reference = NULL,
  visibility = "visible",
  slot = NULL,
  min_zoom = NULL,
  max_zoom = NULL,
  popup = NULL,
  tooltip = NULL,
  tooltip_style = NULL,
  popup_style = NULL,
  hover_options = NULL,
  before_id = NULL,
  filter = NULL
)

Arguments

map

A map object created by the mapboxgl or maplibre functions.

id

A unique ID for the layer.

source

An sf object of points, or the ID of a GeoJSON or vector source.

model_id

The ID of a model registered with add_model(), or an expression that returns one per feature.

source_layer

The source layer (for vector sources).

model_scale

A numeric vector of length 3, c(x, y, z), scaling the model along each axis, or an expression.

model_rotation

A numeric vector of length 3, c(x, y, z), giving rotation around each axis in degrees, or an expression.

model_translation

A numeric vector of length 3, c(x, y, z), giving an offset in metres, or an expression.

model_color

The color to mix into the model's materials.

model_color_mix_intensity

How much of model_color to mix in, from 0 (none) to 1.

model_opacity

The opacity of the model, from 0 to 1.

model_emissive_strength

Emissive strength, used with 3D lights such as those in the Mapbox Standard style.

model_cast_shadows, model_receive_shadows

Logical; whether the model casts and receives shadows.

model_ambient_occlusion_intensity

Ambient occlusion intensity, from 0 to 1.

model_type

"common-3d" (the default) or "location-indicator".

model_elevation_reference

"ground" (the default) to place models on the terrain, or "sea" to measure translation from sea level.

visibility

Whether this layer is displayed.

slot

An optional slot for layer order.

min_zoom

The minimum zoom level for the layer.

max_zoom

The maximum zoom level for the layer.

popup

Popup content shown on click: a column name, a {brace} template (e.g. "{name}: {value}"), or a concat()/number_format() expression. Columns containing HTML are parsed.

tooltip

Tooltip content shown on hover; same forms as popup.

tooltip_style, popup_style

Optional appearance for the tooltip/popup: a preset string ("light" or "dark") or a tooltip_style() object. When omitted, the native (unstyled) appearance is kept.

hover_options

A named list of options for highlighting features in the layer on hover.

before_id

The name of the layer that this layer appears "before", allowing you to insert layers below other layers in your basemap (e.g. labels).

filter

An optional filter expression to subset features in the layer.

Value

The modified map object.

Details

Scale, rotation and translation accept data-driven and zoom-based expressions, so each instance can be sized and oriented from feature attributes. Expressions can't combine separate columns into an array, but an interpolate expression with array outputs can turn one column into a c(x, y, z) value. For a uniform scale taken from a column s: model_scale = list("interpolate", list("linear"), get_column("s"), 0, list("literal", list(0, 0, 0)), 10, list("literal", list(10, 10, 10))).

Mapbox reads glTF models as y-up and converts them to the map's z-up frame, with the model's -z axis pointing north. Feature queries and popups don't reliably register clicks on model geometry; for clickable models, add a transparent add_fill_extrusion_layer() or a circle layer at the same locations and attach the popup there.

Models are drawn in metres: a model whose glTF units are metres appears at real-world size when model_scale is c(1, 1, 1). Instances sit on the terrain when terrain is set with set_terrain().
